**Han Kang** ([Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language"): 한강[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-litencyc-1)) is a South Korean writer. From 2007 to 2018, she taught creative writing at the [Seoul Institute of the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul_Institute_of_the_Arts "Seoul Institute of the Arts").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-2) Han rose to international prominence for her novel _[The Vegetarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Vegetarian "The Vegetarian")_ , which became the first [Korean language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language") novel to win the [International Booker Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Booker_Prize "International Booker Prize") for fiction in 2016. Han is the first Asian woman and Korean to be a recipient of the [Nobel Prize in Literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Literature "Nobel Prize in Literature"), receiving the award in 2024 in recognition of her "intense poetic prose that confronts historical traumas and exposes the fragility of human life".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-3)
## Early life and education
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Han_Kang&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]
Han Kang was born on 27 November 1970 in [Gwangju](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwangju "Gwangju"), South Korea.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-:0-4) According to her father, she is named for the [Han River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_River_\(Korea\) "Han River \(Korea\)") ([Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language"): 한강; [RR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revised_Romanization_of_Korean "Revised Romanization of Korean"): _Hangang_).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-5) Her family is noted for its literary background. Her father is novelist [Han Seung-won](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Seung-won "Han Seung-won"). They made history as the first father and daughter to both be awarded the [Yi Sang Literary Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yi_Sang_Literary_Award "Yi Sang Literary Award").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-6) Her older brother, Han Dong-rim, is also a novelist, while her younger brother, Han Kang-in, is a novelist and cartoonist.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-:0-4)
At the age of nine, Han moved to [Suyu-ri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suyu-dong "Suyu-dong") in [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul "Seoul"), when her father quit his teaching job to become a full-time writer, four months before the [Gwangju Uprising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwangju_Uprising "Gwangju Uprising"), a pro-democracy movement that ended in the military's massacre of students and civilians. She first learned about the massacre when she was 12, after discovering at home a secretly circulated memorial album of photographs taken by a German journalist, [Jürgen Hinzpeter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Hinzpeter "Jürgen Hinzpeter").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-7) This discovery deeply influenced her view on humanity and her literary works.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-litencyc-1)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-8)
Han's father struggled to make ends meet with his writing career, which negatively impacted his family. Han later described her childhood as "too much for a little child"; however, being surrounded by books gave her comfort.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-9) In 1988, she graduated from Poongmoon Girls' High School, now Poongmoon High School, where she had been a class president.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-koreatimes.co.kr-11) In 1993, Han graduated from [Yonsei University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonsei_University "Yonsei University"), where she majored in Korean language and literature.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-litencyc-1) In 1998, she participated in the [University of Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Iowa "University of Iowa") [International Writing Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Writing_Program "International Writing Program") for three months with support from the Arts Council Korea.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-litencyc-1)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-12)
## Career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Han_Kang&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]
After graduating from [Yonsei University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonsei_University "Yonsei University"), Han briefly worked as a reporter for the monthly _Saemteo_ magazine.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-koreatimes.co.kr-11) Han's literary career began the same year when five of her poems, including "Winter in Seoul", were featured in the Winter 1993 issue of the quarterly _Literature and Society_. She made her fiction debut the next year, under the name Han Kang-hyun, when her short story "The Scarlet Anchor" won the New Year's Literary Contest held by the _[Seoul Shinmun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul_Shinmun "Seoul Shinmun")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-14) Her first short story collection, _A Love of Yeosu_ , was published in 1995 and attracted attention for its precise and tightly narrated structure. After the publication, she quit her magazine job to solely focus on writing literature.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-15)
In 2007, Han published a book, _A Song to Sing Calmly_ (가만가만 부르는 노래[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-16) The same year, she started working as a professor in the Department of Creative Writing at the [Seoul Institute of the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul_Institute_of_the_Arts "Seoul Institute of the Arts") until 2018.
In her college years Han became obsessed with a line of poetry by the Korean modernist poet [Yi Sang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yi_Sang "Yi Sang"): "I believe that humans should be plants."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-donga-17) She understood Yi's line to imply a defensive stance against the violence of [Korea's colonial history under Japanese occupation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korea_under_Japanese_rule "Korea under Japanese rule") and took it as an inspiration to write her most successful work, _The Vegetarian_. The second part of the three-part novel, _Mongolian Mark_ , won the [Yi Sang Literary Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yi_Sang_Literary_Award "Yi Sang Literary Award").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-WhiteReview-18) The rest of the series (_The Vegetarian_ and _Fire Tree_) was delayed by contractual problems.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-donga-17)
_The Vegetarian_ was Han's first novel translated into English, although she had already attracted worldwide attention by the time [Deborah Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deborah_Smith_\(translator\) "Deborah Smith \(translator\)") translated it.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-Khakpour-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-20) The translated work won the [International Booker Prize 2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Booker_Prize#2016 "International Booker Prize") for both Han and Smith. Han was the first Korean writer to be nominated for the award, and _The Vegetarian_ was the first [Korean language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language") novel to win the [International Booker Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Booker_Prize "International Booker Prize") for fiction.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-:1-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-NewYorker2018-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-BBC17May16-24) _The Vegetarian_ was also chosen as one of "The 10 Best Books of 2016" by _[The New York Times Book Review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times_Book_Review "The New York Times Book Review")_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-25)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Han_Kang_-_2017.png/250px-Han_Kang_-_2017.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Han_Kang_-_2017.png)Han Kang in 2017
Han's novel _[Human Acts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Acts "Human Acts")_ was released in January 2016 by Portobello Books.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-portobello-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-telegraphs_human-27) Han received the [Premio Malaparte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premio_Malaparte "Premio Malaparte") for the Italian translation of _Human Acts_ , _Atti Umani_ , by Adelphi Edizioni, in Italy on 1 October 2017.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-:2-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-:3-29) The English translation of the novel was shortlisted for the 2018 [International Dublin Literary Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Dublin_Literary_Award "International Dublin Literary Award").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-30)
Han's third novel, _The White Book_ , was shortlisted for the 2018 [International Booker Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Booker_Prize "International Booker Prize").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-31) An autobiographical novel, it centers on the loss of her older sister, a baby who died two hours after her birth.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-Beckerman-32)
Han's novel _We Do Not Part_ was published in 2021. It tells the story of a writer researching the 1948–49 [Jeju uprising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeju_uprising "Jeju uprising") and its impact on her friend's family. The French translation of the novel won the [Prix Médicis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prix_M%C3%A9dicis "Prix Médicis") Étranger in 2023.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-guardian_nobel-33)
In 2023, Han's fourth full-length novel, _Greek Lessons_ , was translated into English by Deborah Smith and E Yaewon.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-34) _[The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Atlantic "The Atlantic")_ magazine called it a book in which "words are both insufficient and too powerful to tame".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-35)
In 2024, Han's short story "Heavy Snow" was published by the 18 November 2024 issue of _[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_Yorker "The New Yorker")._[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-36)
In 2025, Han was among 414 South Korean writers who were signatories to a petition urging the [Constitutional Court of Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Court_of_Korea "Constitutional Court of Korea") to uphold the [impeachment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_of_Yoon_Suk_Yeol "Impeachment of Yoon Suk Yeol") of suspended president [Yoon Suk Yeol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoon_Suk_Yeol "Yoon Suk Yeol") over his [martial law declaration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_South_Korean_martial_law_crisis "2024 South Korean martial law crisis").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-37)
## Personal life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Han_Kang&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]
Han was married to Hong Yong-hee, a literary critic and professor at [Kyung Hee Cyber University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyung_Hee_Cyber_University "Kyung Hee Cyber University").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-39) In 2024, Han stated that they had been divorced for many years.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-40)[_[unreliable source?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")_][[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-41) Han has a son, and they ran a bookstore in Seoul together from 2018 to November 2024, when she stepped down from its management.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-43) The bookstore closed in 2026.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-44)
Han has said that she suffers from periodic [migraines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Migraines "Migraines") and credits them with "keeping her humble".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-Beckerman-32)
## Awards and recognition
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Han_Kang&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Awards and recognition")]
Han won the [Yi Sang Literary Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yi_Sang_Literary_Award "Yi Sang Literary Award") (2005) for _Mongolian Mark_ (the second part of _The Vegetarian_),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-WhiteReview-18) the 25th Korean Novelist Award for her novella _Baby Buddha_ in 1999, the 2000 Today's Young Artist Award from the [Korean Ministry of Culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Culture,_Sports_and_Tourism_\(South_Korea\) "Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism \(South Korea\)"), and the 2010 Dongri Literary Award for _The Wind is Blowing_.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-website_bio-45)
In 2018, Han became the fifth writer chosen to contribute to _[Future Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Future_Library "Future Library")_. [Katie Paterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katie_Paterson "Katie Paterson"), the project's organizer, said that Han had been chosen because she "expands our view of the world".[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-46) Han delivered the manuscript, _Dear Son, My Beloved_ , in May 2019. In the handover ceremony, she dragged a white cloth through the forest and wrapped it around the manuscript. She explained this as a reference to Korean culture, in which a white cloth is used both for babies and for mourning gowns, describing the event as "like a wedding of my manuscript with this forest. Or a lullaby for a century-long sleep".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-47)
Han was elected a [Royal Society of Literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Society_of_Literature "Royal Society of Literature") International Writer in 2023, recognizing her significant contributions to global literature and the impact of her works beyond South Korea.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-50)
_The Vegetarian_ placed 49th in _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_ 's "100 Best Books of the 21st century" in July 2024.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-51)
### Nobel Prize in Literature
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Han_Kang&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Nobel Prize in Literature")]
Main article: [2024 Nobel Prize in Literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Nobel_Prize_in_Literature "2024 Nobel Prize in Literature")
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b6/Han_Kang%2C_2024_Nobel_Prize_Laureate_in_Literature_10.jpg/250px-Han_Kang%2C_2024_Nobel_Prize_Laureate_in_Literature_10.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Han_Kang,_2024_Nobel_Prize_Laureate_in_Literature_10.jpg)Han Kang at the press conference in Stockholm during the Nobel week in December 2024
In 2024, Han was awarded the [Nobel Prize in Literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Literature "Nobel Prize in Literature") by the [Swedish Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_Academy "Swedish Academy") for her "intense poetic prose that confronts historical traumas and exposes the fragility of human life".[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-:0_1-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-:0_2-53)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-guardian_nobel-33) This made her the first Korean writer and the first female Asian writer to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-55) The awarding was widely celebrated in South Korea,[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-56) while [international reactions were mixed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Nobel_Prize_in_Literature#International_reactions "2024 Nobel Prize in Literature").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-58) Han herself said she was surprised but honoured by the recognition.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-nob-59) Han delivered her [Nobel lecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_lecture "Nobel lecture"), titled _Light and Thread,_ on 7 December 2024 at the Swedish Academy in Stockholm.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-61)

## Adaptations
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Han_Kang&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Adaptations")]
_Baby Buddha_ and _The Vegetarian_ have been made into films. Lim Woo-Seong wrote and directed _[Vegetarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vegetarian_\(film\) "Vegetarian \(film\)")_ , which was released in 2009.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-82) It was one of only 14 selections (out of 1,022 submissions) included in the World Narrative Competition of the North American Film Fest, and was noticed at the [Busan International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Busan_International_Film_Festival "Busan International Film Festival").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-nobel_biobiblio-83)
Lim also adapted _Baby Buddha_ into a screenplay, in collaboration with Han, and directed the film version. Titled _Scars_ , it was released in 2011.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_Kang#cite_note-nobel_biobiblio-83)
